title: Controlled Strain of 3D Hydrogels under Live Microscopy Imaging
protocol: Add 38 μL of 10 mg/mL succinimidyl ester fluorescent dye dissolved in DMSO to 1.5 mL of 15 mg/mL fibrinogen solution (molar ratio of 5:1) in a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Place the tube on a shaker for 1 hour at room temperature.
Centrifuge the tube for 3 minutes at 800 x g at room temperature.
Pre-wash the desalting column with 25 mL of fibrinogen buffer.
Slowly inject the labeled-fibrinogen into the pre-washed desalting column, ensuring no bubbles enter the filter.
Discard the first ~0.3 mL of eluted solution (4-6 drops of faint colored liquid).
Collect the following 1.0-1.5 mL of purified solution as per manufacturer’s protocol.
Sterilize the resulting purified solution using a syringe-driven filter (0.22-0.45 μm).
Divide the resulting purified labeled-fibrinogen into small aliquots of ~7-50 μL and store in a -20 °C freezer.
Store approximately 7 μL of the purified labeled fibrinogen in the refrigerator (4 °C) until step 4.
Prepare 7 μL of thrombin solution by diluting using thrombin buffer to 2 units/mL and keep it in the refrigerator (4 °C) until step 4.
Reconstitute fluorescent spherical beads according to manufacturer's instructions.
Mix thrombin solution with fluorescent beads in a ratio of 1:25 v/v % when internal strain measurements are desired.
Retrieve 0.5 mm thick silicone rubber and cut into 15 x 80 mm² strips.
Cut a 2 mm diameter hole in the center of each silicone strip.
Cover both sides of silicone with original plastic wrapping if available.
Treat reused silicone strips with trypsin for 0.5 hour.
Soak treated silicone strips in 0.2 M NaOH for 0.5 hour.
Soak NaOH-treated silicone strips in 70% ethanol for 1 hour.
Dry treated silicone strips before use.
Prepare hydrophobic sealing film layers measuring at least 20 x 30 mm².
Wash a 10 cm dish with 70% ethanol.
Wipe and dry the dish with non-linting delicate task wipes.
Place two strips side-by-side in the washed 10 cm dish.
Remove the plastic wrap from one side of the silicone strip.
Place the exposed side of the silicone strip on the sealing film layer so it surrounds the cut-out area entirely.
Press gently on the silicone against the sealing film layer to seal the surrounding area, using clean gloved fingers.
Ensure there are no air-pockets between the silicone and the sealing film, especially around the cut-out.
Place the silicone strips & sealing film layers in 70% ethanol overnight.
Perform UV sterilization for 30 minutes on each side of the sterilized materials.
Sterilize 10 cm dishes under UV light for 30 minutes after a 70% ethanol wash if not already sterile.
Perform an autoclave sterilization cycle on the silicone strips (140 °C) if necessary.
Determine cell concentration by performing a cell count.
Centrifuge and re-suspend the cell pellet with 7 μL of thrombin (2 units/mL).
Keep cells chilled until use, avoiding exposure for more than half an hour to prevent damage.
Retrieve 2 Unit/mL thrombin solution from refrigerator and place on ice.
Retrieve 10 mg/mL labeled-fibrinogen solution from refrigerator and place on ice.
Extract 2.5 μL of labeled-fibrinogen.
Pipette the fibrinogen uniformly into the silicone cut-out so that the entire circumference is in contact with fibrinogen.
Take 2.5 μL of thrombin (with or without cells/beads).
Pipette the thrombin directly into the fibrinogen solution in the cut-out, reaching a final volume of 5 μL fibrin.
Carefully pipette up and down about 10 times to mix the two solutions.
Move the tip around the entire volume during mixing to create as homogenous a solution as possible.
Add a very small amount of Phosphate Buffer Saline (PBS) or cell medium along the edge of each dish.
Cover the dish(es).
Place the covered dishes in the incubator at 37 °C for 30 minutes.
Remove the dish(es) from the incubator after the incubation period.
Add PBS/cell medium to the dish, submerging the entire gel-silicone construct.
Carefully lift the sample constructs one at a time from the dish.
Ensure that the sealing film layer remains adhered to the strip.
Gently peel the sealing film layer from one end of the silicone to the other, avoiding areas close to the cut-out.
Avoid contact with the cut-out to prevent damage to the sample.
Place the strip back into the dish containing PBS/cell medium so it floats in the solution.
Take the dish(es) to a standard cell-culture microscope for qualitative assessment.
Ensure gels are uniform and continuous throughout the cut-out, free of bubbles.
Select the best samples based on their condition for further analysis.
Fill the bath with PBS/cell medium.
Place the silicone strip carrying the sample gel across the top so the ends are sitting on each side of the bath.
Tighten the clamps along with the fabric strips so that all pieces are connected to form one straight strip with the cut-out in the center.
Retrieve the SCyUS device and attach the aluminum liquid well.
Attach a 22 mm x 40 mm rectangular glass coverslip (No. 1 or 1.5) to the bottom of the well using sealing material.
Fill the well with ~1-2 mL of PBS/cell medium.
Place the strip + fabric + gel construct into the device.
Clamp the fabric strip into the bracket so that the cut-out + gel is in the center.
Carefully place the pin-down insert into the device and lock it in place.
Insert the other fabric side to the spindle without attaching the servomotor, then lock it into the spindle.
Insert the SCyUS device with the attached sample into the stage of the microscope.
Connect the microcontroller to the computer via a USB cable.
Connect the servomotor to the microcontroller.
Open the SCyUS control module on the computer.
Ensure adequate gel for sampling.
Take a low-magnification confocal Z-stack tile image of the entire gel using lasers of 488/543/561.
Scan the gel and determine the lowest Z-position where full adhesion to the inner walls of the cut-out is apparent with no tears or bubbles, noting the Z-location (Zl).
Move up in the Z-direction until there is no longer continuity in the gel and note the upper limit Z-position (Zu).
Subtract the upper limit (Zu) from the lower limit (Zl) to determine the reference thickness of the sample (Zo).
Determine the pre-stretched position of the sample using live imaging under the confocal microscope.
Make sure the servomotor is at its zero position by clicking the Go To Zero Servo Pos button.
Attach the servomotor to the stretching device as seen in Figure 6C.
Do this step slowly and carefully to avoid putting excess tension on the sample.
Move the motor one degree at a time in the clockwise direction by clicking the +1 button until the right side of the cut-out is observed moving.
Reverse the movement back to the penultimate step position by clicking on the -1 button.
Set the reference position by clicking on the Set Min Servo Position button.
Return to the reference position at any time by clicking the Go To Min Servo Position button.
Use a high-magnification objective (≥40×) for this step to minimize error.
Capture a high-magnification (40×), high-resolution (~0.2 μm × 0.2 μm pixel size), single Z-slice tile image of the entire gel area.
Capture a single Z-slice image in the middle of the gel thickness (by using Zo from Eq. 1).
Adjust the servomotor to the desired stretch magnitude by advancing one degree at a time in the GUI, slowly (about 1 degree/second).
Capture a single Z-slice high-resolution tile image of the entire gel area for post-processing analysis.
Scan the interface between the gel and the silicone to verify that the gel has not detached throughout its circumference.
Recalculate Zo (Eq. 1) for each stretch magnitude to adjust the Z-position of the microscope to the approximate center of the gel thickness.
Adjust the Z-position of the microscope during stretching to account for the Z-Poisson effect where the bottom of the gel rises.
Define the largest distance from top to bottom as the perpendicular distance.
Repeat this process for all stretch interval images.
Calculate the axial and perpendicular distances of the cut-out periphery.
Perform calculations to find the strains of the cut-out edges.
Capture a high-resolution Z-stack image of the selected ROI in the pre-stretch position.
Return to the same ROI after each desired stretch interval and repeat the image capture process.
Import images into ImageJ.
Record the X-Y pixel location of each visible bead aggregate in the ROI.
Transfer recorded data to a spreadsheet.
Measure distances between every pair of aggregates.
Compare measured distances with those from the reference image to calculate strains in the X and Y directions.
